meta.title: ANATOMY OF A VERDICT
meta.grammar: Concession (although, despite, even so, adjective + as)
meta.style: Painted digital illustration in muted oil tones, soft brush edges, no hard outlines; an English Crown Court jury room and a converted stone mill on a rainy October afternoon: slate blue, oatmeal, faded oxblood and brass, with one warm lamp glow on the key object in every frame; eye-level camera, three-quarter view; 3:2

cover.title: ANATOMY OF A VERDICT
cover.lead: Ruth Adair's husband fell down the iron stairs of their mill. Eleven jurors say she pushed him. You are juror twelve, and you are not sure.
cover.small: Single player · C1 · two forks, four endings

hotspot.object: the empty twelfth chair at the jury table

briefing.title: HOW TO CONCEDE A POINT

cards.head: ALTHOUGH / EVEN THOUGH + CLAUSE
cards.text: Although she was angry, nobody saw her push him.

cards.head: DESPITE / IN SPITE OF + NOUN OR -ING
cards.text: Despite the shouting, the recording proves nothing.

cards.head: EVEN SO / STILL / AND YET
cards.text: She lied about the time. Even so, that isn't murder.

cards.head: ADJECTIVE + AS / THOUGH + CLAUSE
cards.text: Strange as it sounds, the rail was already loose.

cards.head: MAY ... BUT / MUCH AS + CLAUSE
cards.text: She may have been furious, but furious isn't guilty.

briefing.note: Concede the point first, then turn it. Never ALTHOUGH ... BUT in one sentence, and never DESPITE + a subject and verb.

hotspot.object: the ballot slips under the lamp

room1.title: ELEVEN TO ONE
room1.story: Gerald Pryce, the foreman, counts the slips. "Eleven guilty. One not guilty." Every head turns towards you.
room1.clue: Ruth was shouting at Simon the day before. You still have doubts.
room1.prompt: Which sentence states your position correctly?

answers.text: Although she shouted, I'm not sure.
Although she shouted, but I'm not sure.
Despite she shouted, I'm not sure.

room1.explanation: ALTHOUGH + a clause needs no BUT after it. DESPITE takes a noun or -ING, never a full clause like 'she shouted'.

room2.title: THE CABBIE
room2.story: Danny Rourke drives a cab and has an opinion on everything. "She was angry. He's dead. Job done."
room2.clue: You accept that she was angry. Anger alone proves nothing.
room2.prompt: ___ her anger, it doesn't prove she pushed him.
room2.explanation: A noun phrase follows the gap, so you need DESPITE. ALTHOUGH and EVEN THOUGH need a clause: 'although she was angry'.

room3.title: THE HEADTEACHER
room3.story: Agnes Bell, a retired headteacher, has filled four pages in pencil. She looks up. "Go on, then. Convince me."
room3.clue: Ruth lied to the police about when she left. You can't deny it.
room3.prompt: Which sentence concedes the lie, then turns it?

answers.text: She lied. Even though, a lie isn't a push.
She lied. Despite, a lie isn't a push.
She lied. Even so, a lie isn't a push.

room3.explanation: EVEN SO is an adverb that opens a new sentence. EVEN THOUGH and DESPITE are linkers and need something after them.

room4.title: THE RECORDING PLAYS
room4.story: The usher brings in the laptop. Simon's phone recording plays again: shouting, a crash, then Ruth crying.
room4.clue: You are a sound engineer. The crash is very hard to place.
room4.prompt: ___ hard I listen, I can't tell what crashed.
room4.explanation: HOWEVER + adjective or adverb + clause means 'it makes no difference how': however hard I listen. ALTHOUGH can't take 'hard' next.

hotspot.object: the photo of the bruised arm

room5.title: THE NURSE
room5.story: Priya Sandhu works nights in A&E. "I've seen a hundred falls. That bruise on his arm worries me."
room5.clue: The bruise worries her. The stair rail had been loose for months.

answers.text: Worrying as is it, the rail was loose.
Worrying as it is, the rail was loose.
Worrying although it is, the rail was loose.

room5.explanation: ADJECTIVE + AS + clause concedes a point: worrying as it is = although it is worrying. The subject comes before the verb.

room6.title: THE FOREMAN'S TRAIN
room6.story: Gerald checks his watch. "Look, I respect you. But it's eleven to one, and I've a train at six."
room6.clue: You respect Gerald too. You still want the evidence looked at again.
room6.prompt: ___ I respect you, we have to look again.
room6.explanation: MUCH AS + clause is a formal ALTHOUGH, often with like or respect. DESPITE needs a noun; EVEN alone isn't a linker.

rec1.title: THE SHOUTING
rec1.story: Headphones on. Ruth's voice: "You never finish anything!" Then Simon, laughing. Danny leans in. "Hear that? Furious."
rec1.clue: She sounds furious. Yet Simon is laughing, so he wasn't afraid.
rec1.prompt: She ___ furious, but Simon wasn't afraid of her.
rec1.explanation: MAY HAVE + past participle concedes a past possibility before BUT turns it. After a modal comes HAVE, never HAD or HAS.

hotspot.object: the photo of the broken rail

stair1.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHS
stair1.story: Priya spreads the police photos under the lamp. Iron stairs, a high gallery, a rail hanging from one bolt.
stair1.clue: The rail is broken. The prosecution says Ruth broke it in a struggle.
stair1.prompt: Which sentence answers the prosecution correctly?

answers.text: It's broken. Although, nobody knows when.
It's broken. That said, nobody knows when.
It's broken. That saying, nobody knows when.

stair1.explanation: THAT SAID at the start of a sentence concedes the point before it. ALTHOUGH can't stand alone before a comma.

hotspot.object: the mill kitchen in the flashback

rec2.title: THE CRASH
rec2.story: You loop the crash five times. The echo is long: it happened far from the phone, near the kitchen.
rec2.clue: Ruth's voice is close to the phone at the very moment of the crash.
rec2.prompt: Which sentence makes your point correctly?

answers.text: Loud though it is, she's nowhere near it.
Though loud it is, she's nowhere near it.
Loud despite it is, she's nowhere near it.

rec2.explanation: ADJECTIVE + THOUGH + clause works like ADJECTIVE + AS: loud though it is. The adjective comes first, then THOUGH.

stair2.title: THE BRUISE
stair2.story: Priya grips her own arm. "A hand makes a mark like that. So does a rail, if you grab it as you fall."
stair2.clue: You try every way to read the bruise as a grip. It still fits a fall.
stair2.prompt: ___ I might, I can't make it a push.
stair2.explanation: VERB + AS + subject + MIGHT concedes effort that failed: try as I might = although I try hard. Use the base verb.

rec3.title: THE MISSING MINUTE
rec3.story: The file is shorter than it should be. Fifty-eight seconds are missing between the crash and the crying.
rec3.clue: Nobody knows who cut it. It could have been Simon himself.
rec3.prompt: ___ the gap, the court accepted the recording.
rec3.explanation: IN SPITE OF + noun: in spite of the gap. Never IN SPITE without OF; EVEN THOUGH needs a subject and verb.

stair3.title: THE EXPERIMENT
stair3.story: Priya stands on a chair, holds her arm out at gallery height, then lets it drop. "If he grabbed the rail... yes."
stair3.clue: Priya had doubts about a fall. Her experiment answers most of them.
stair3.prompt: Priya: "___ my doubts, a fall fits the injuries."
stair3.explanation: FOR ALL + noun = despite: for all my doubts. ALTHOUGH needs a clause, and IN SPITE needs OF.

rec4.title: DANNY GOES QUIET
rec4.story: You play Danny the echo, then the gap. He is quiet for once. "All right. It's not as clear as I thought."
rec4.clue: Danny still thinks she's capable of it. But he admits there's doubt.
rec4.prompt: Danny: "___ she's capable of it, I can't be certain."
rec4.explanation: WHILE + clause can concede: while she's capable of it = although. WHEREAS compares two facts; NEVERTHELESS opens a new clause.

hotspot.object: the photo of the rusted bolt

stair4.title: THE RUSTED BOLT
stair4.story: In the photo the bolt is rusted through. In March Simon emailed a builder about the rail. He never booked him.
stair4.clue: Ruth may or may not have been on the stairs. The rail was dangerous anyway.
stair4.prompt: Which sentence states the point correctly?

answers.text: Even though she was there, it was unsafe.
Even she was there, it was unsafe.
Even if she was there, it was unsafe.

stair4.explanation: EVEN IF: we don't know whether she was there. EVEN THOUGH would treat it as fact. EVEN alone isn't a linker.

after1.title: ARTY TYPES
after1.story: Lunch arrives in plastic boxes. Victor Lane, a landlord, hasn't touched his. "Arty types. They all lie."
after1.clue: Victor has judged her by her job, not the evidence. You keep calm.
after1.prompt: ___ your feelings about artists, look at the facts.
after1.explanation: WHATEVER + noun concedes any possibility: whatever your feelings = it makes no difference what they are. HOWEVER needs an adjective.

after2.title: THE SECOND VOTE
after2.story: Gerald calls a second vote. Nine guilty, three not guilty. Victor slams the table. "This is ridiculous."
after2.clue: The vote has moved. Victor is just as certain as before.
after2.explanation: REGARDLESS OF + noun = it makes no difference: regardless of the vote. The preposition is OF, never TO.

after3.title: AT THE WINDOW
after3.story: You stand at the window with Agnes. Rain on the car park. "He's not a bad man," she says. "Just tired."
after3.clue: Victor is rude. Agnes thinks he deserves a hearing anyway.
after3.prompt: Agnes: "He's rude. ___, he deserves a hearing."
after3.explanation: STILL at the start of a sentence concedes the last point: still, he deserves a hearing. ALTHOUGH and DESPITE must join to something.

wit1.title: KIT'S STATEMENT
wit1.story: Kit Marlow, the apprentice, told the court he heard "a scream, then a thud" from the stairwell at half past two.
wit1.clue: Kit sounded honest. He was also wearing headphones at the wheel.
wit1.prompt: Which sentence is fair to Kit?

answers.text: He may honest, but he had headphones on.
He may be honest, but he had headphones on.
He may is honest, but he had headphones on.

wit1.explanation: MAY + base verb ... BUT concedes, then turns: he may be honest, but. MAY never takes IS, and BE can't be dropped.

hotspot.object: the white van in the lane

clock1.title: THE WHITE VAN
clock1.story: A neighbour's doorbell camera shows Ruth's van leaving the mill at 14:25. Her 999 call comes at 14:52.
clock1.clue: Simon died between two and three, so the times don't clear her.
clock1.prompt: Which sentence concedes the point correctly?

answers.text: It isn't proof. And yet it matters.
It isn't proof. Although it matters.
It isn't proof. Despite it matters.

clock1.explanation: AND YET can open a new sentence. 'Although it matters' has no main clause, and DESPITE can't take a subject and verb.

wit2.title: EXHIBIT FOURTEEN
wit2.story: Exhibit 14: Kit's headphones, found on the wheel. You know this model. It blocks out almost everything.
wit2.clue: Kit's music was loud. A scream might still get through, just about.
wit2.prompt: ___ loud the music was, a scream might get through.
wit2.explanation: NO MATTER HOW + adjective + clause: no matter how loud the music was. Loud is an adjective, so there's no MUCH.

clock2.title: TWELVE MINUTES
clock2.story: The van's satnav was read out in court: twelve minutes to the clay merchant, twelve back, one stop on the way.
clock2.clue: She could have driven fast. The satnav says she kept to the limit.
clock2.prompt: ___ she could have driven fast, the satnav says not.
clock2.explanation: THOUGH + clause = although: though she could have driven fast. EVEN alone isn't a linker; IN SPITE OF needs a noun.

wit3.title: GERALD LISTENS
wit3.story: Gerald puts on the headphones himself and plays music. Agnes screams behind him. Gerald doesn't turn round.
wit3.clue: Gerald heard almost nothing. He wanted to go home. Now he wants it right.
wit3.prompt: Gerald: "___ to go home, I'm changing my vote."
wit3.explanation: DESPITE + -ING: despite wanting to go home. Never DESPITE + subject and verb, and never DESPITE OF.

clock3.title: IT DOESN'T ADD UP
clock3.story: Gerald takes off his watch and lays it on the table. "Twelve there, twelve back, and a stop. It doesn't add up."
clock3.clue: Gerald's train matters to him. The timeline matters more now.
clock3.prompt: Gerald: "___ my train, I'll stay until we're sure."
clock3.explanation: IN SPITE OF + noun: in spite of my train. IN SPITE needs OF; EVEN THOUGH needs a subject and verb.

vote1.title: ELEVEN TO ONE AGAIN
vote1.story: It's eleven to one again, the other way. Victor looks at his hands. "My son walked out too. Never said why."
vote1.clue: Victor is hurting. You understand him, and you still need his vote.
vote1.prompt: ___ I understand, this isn't about your son.
vote1.explanation: AS MUCH AS + clause concedes a feeling: as much as I understand. Both ASes are needed; SO MUCH AS means something else.

hotspot.object: the last slip in Victor's hand

vote2.title: THE LAST BALLOT
vote2.story: The usher knocks. Gerald holds out his hand for the slips. Victor's is the last to go onto the pile.
vote2.clue: You'll never know what happened on those stairs. The doubt is reasonable.
vote2.prompt: Which sentence closes the case correctly?

answers.text: Although we can't know, but we must decide.
Although we can't know, we must decide.
Despite we can't know, we must decide.

vote2.explanation: ALTHOUGH + clause, then the main clause, with no BUT. DESPITE can't take 'we can't know': it needs a noun or -ING.

hotspot.object: the evidence trolley by the door

evidence.title: WHAT DO WE REOPEN?
evidence.story: Gerald gives in. "One piece of evidence, then we vote again. Your choice." Two exhibits wait on the court trolley.

choices.label: REPLAY THE RECORDING
choices.note: Your trade. Every second, every echo, every gap.

choices.label: STUDY THE STAIRWELL
choices.note: Priya's trade. The photographs, the rail, the fall.

hotspot.object: the two exhibit folders under the lamp

doubt.title: WHERE DOES THE DOUBT LIE?
doubt.story: Victor folds his arms. "Give me one reason." You have two: the apprentice who heard them, or the doorbell camera across the lane.

choices.label: QUESTION THE WITNESS
choices.note: Kit Marlow, nineteen, the apprentice. He says he heard a scream.

choices.label: RUN THE CLOCK
choices.note: A doorbell camera, a white van, a 999 call. Twenty-seven minutes.

master.label: UNANIMOUS
master.title: NOT GUILTY, TWELVE TO NONE
master.text: Twelve slips, one word. Ruth Adair grips the rail of the dock and does not cry. You will never know what happened on those stairs. That was the point: nobody in that room could know.

hotspot.object: Ruth's hands on the brass rail of the dock

complete.label: VERDICT REACHED
complete.title: NOT GUILTY
complete.text: Eleven to one is enough after this long, the judge says. Victor would not move, and maybe he never could. Ruth walks out into the rain, and you walk out behind her.

hotspot.object: the open court doors in the rain

missing.label: HUNG JURY
missing.title: NO VERDICT
missing.text: Four hours, three votes, and the room never settles. The judge discharges you. There will be a retrial, a new twelve, the same recording. You hope one of them knows what an echo is.

failed.label: OUT OF CHANCES
failed.title: ELEVEN BECOME TWELVE
failed.text: Your arguments came out wrong and the room stopped listening. At five to six you raise your hand with the others. Gerald catches his train. You lie awake for a long time.
